title: Commercial Bank Examination Manual, 3000—Capital, Earnings, Liquidity, and Sensitivity to Market Risk
summary: This Federal Reserve examination manual (Section 3000) provides procedural guidance for bank examiners on assessing capital adequacy, earnings, liquidity, and market risk sensitivity at state member banks. The document describes Regulation Q (12 CFR Part 217) capital requirements adopted in 2013, detailing the three-tier capital framework (Common Equity Tier 1, Additional Tier 1, and Tier 2 capital) used to evaluate whether banking organizations maintain sufficient capital to absorb losses and continue lending during economic stress.
key_points: Regulation Q (12 CFR Part 217) was adopted in 2013 by the Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC to replace general risk-based capital requirements and address weaknesses highlighted during the 2008-09 financial crisis
The three components of regulatory capital are: (1) Common Equity Tier 1 capital, (2) Additional Tier 1 capital, and (3) Tier 2 capital
Common Equity Tier 1 capital represents the highest-quality and most loss-absorbing form of capital, primarily composed of common stock and retained earnings
The risk-based capital ratio is calculated by dividing qualifying capital (numerator) by risk-weighted assets (denominator)
Capital adequacy triggers the most supervisory action under the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) provisions of section 38 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1831o)
Regulation Q applies to state member banks, U.S.-domiciled bank holding companies, and covered savings and loan holding companies on a consolidated basis
why_it_matters: This document is an internal examination manual for bank regulators, not a market-moving release or macroeconomic analysis. It codifies how Federal Reserve examiners evaluate whether banks have sufficient capital buffers. While important for understanding bank supervision, it does not contain time-sensitive market intelligence or macro catalyst information relevant to trading decisions.
